Notion Custom Agents help our team go beyond doing work with AI to building AI tools that do the work for them.
I'm always disappointed by note-taking tools calling themselves a Notion alternative when they do not provide an alternative to Notion... e.g. the database functionality.
I really appreciate how Notion is basically "what if Google Docs but you can actually organize your information". The collaborative components feel really powerful.

Notion feels like it's got this serious range from individuals up to teams at large enterprises. It's incredibly flexible and configurable... it was so interesting to watch it eat away at other things like Confluence over the years.
Google Docs on steroids. I approve of it.
I was happily giving them $4/month after running out of space in their trial plan, and now I absolutely have no reason to keep giving them money.

The one thing that bothers me about Notion... is the lack of encryption... whenever there is a free tier without a form of end-to-end encryption in place, it feels like a data puddle waiting to become a lake.
Notion is the embodiment of busy work --> false sense of being productive.
Notion consuming 10-15% CPU while on idle is a deal breaker to me. I wish they'd devote a bit more resources to fix this. (On macOS)
If they only had a native Mac application. I love Notion, but the Mac client feels so sluggish, looks like a web view or Electron or something similar.

Notion is currently a jack of all trades and master of none. We have tried to use it as a wiki, project tracker, issue tracker, CRM & spreadsheet... we quickly reach limits of what is possible automatically.

I mentioned this before. Notion is great, but the fact that they use fullstory (session recording) for a note taking app is a huge problem for me... I especially dislike that they don't disclose session recording upfront.

We use it to keep track of all of our tasks and projects... notifications are still hit or miss despite talking to support about it multiple times... I'd love it if the Mac app was native instead of electron based.
I've started using notion as a kind of personal wiki... My only issue with Notion is that I feel it's hard to get stuff out of it, especially on mobile.
We use them in lieu of JIRA. Overall I like the product! I wish they had ticket numbers... I had to hack them in using timestamps and hashes.

For me, Notion replaced Evernote and I haven't looked back. Three features that have been particularly useful: Kanban board-ing, collapsible blocks, and substantially smoother linking to, or embedding, notes within notes.

I love the product, but the login workflow is awful... the login is a randomly-generated one-time code sent to your email address... Notion is unusable on my mobile device since I have no email on it.
There is something about Notion that makes it feel very well-made and coherent... On the flip side the software is a bit slow to start and uses a lot of resources—it's based on Electron.
I love Notion but the speed, or rather lack of, is killing me daily. Last Friday I was taking some notes, and suddenly the page refreshed and everything was gone.
Notion could as well but they are a slow moving beast with different priorities.
Accessibility in both Notion and Confluence is absolutely abysmal.
